previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for worsening chronic back pain and abdominal discomfort. His back pain, described as a constant burning sensation in the mid-thoracic region, was evaluated with imaging including a chest MRA and thoracic spine X-ray, both of which showed no acute abnormalities. The pain was deemed likely musculoskeletal, and his pain regimen was optimized with increased acetaminophen and addition of tizanidine. Abdominal bloating and pain were attributed to newly diagnosed pancreatic insufficiency, confirmed by stool testing, and he was started on Creon. His kidney function remained stable, immunosuppressive and chronic disease medications were continued, and he was discharged home with follow-up arranged with his primary care provider and gastroenterologist.

Brief Hospital Course:
PATIENT SUMMARY FOR ADMISSION:
===============================
Mr. ___ is a ___ male with past medical history 
significant for ESRD ___ diabetic nephropathy s/p failed LRRT in 
___ and active DDRT in ___ with progressive kidney failure 
secondary to hypertension, diabetic calciphylaxis requiring 
lower extremity BKA, OSA, PVD s/p revascularization, HTN, CAD, 
who presented with subacute worsening of chronic chest pain. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
====================
[] Stop leflunomide.
[] Consideration of further anti-hypertensives as he was quite 
hypertensive throughout admission. 
[] Continued management of chest pain and attempts to wean 
opioid use.
[] If persistent chest pain, consider TTE to evaluated for heart 
failure as he appeared clinically overloaded and we considered 
fluid overload as a potential etiology. 

ACUTE/ACTIVE ISSUES:
====================
# Atypical chest pain:
Subacute on chronic substernal chest pain radiating to back that 
has been ongoing for past ___ months and has been previously 
evaluated. ACS ruled out with flat MB, no EKG changes. MRA in 
___ as outpatient with no evidence of aortic dissection. His 
chest pain is otherwise non-exertional, he can tolerate stairs 
with no complaints, not related to eating, and largely 
non-positional. He identified no aggravating or alleviating 
conditions. We did consider GI etiologies as he had esophageal 
thickening and gastric thickening on a previous CT, so we 
consulted GI. EGD did not show any gross abnormalities, although 
biopsies were consistent with gastritis. GI recommended 
initiation of high-dose PPI for 3 months and then re-evaluation 
with transition to low-dose as needed. We did give diuresis for 
1 day given evidence of fluid overload and some concern that 
chest pain was the result of congestion, but creatinine became 
elevated and we did not further volume reduce per Renal 
Transplant recommendations. Further consideration of this can be 
given as an outpatient, and a TTE can be considered. There was 
brief consideration of chronic pancreatitis, but this was not 
further evaluated as there was no CT evidence previously. We 
continued his gabapentin and oxycodone. 

# Hypertension:
Remained hypertensive, at times with SBP > 200. Per renal recs, 
will discontinue losartan and switch to hydralazine 25mg TID 
with further titration as an outpatient. 

# ESRD s/p DDRT ___:
History of failed renal transplant with DDRT in ___ complicated 
by FSGS and IFTSA on biopsy in ___ with concern for worsening 
in the setting of HTN and diabetic nephropathy. Transplant 
Nephrology followed the patient and a renal US was obtained and 
reviewed. We continued tacroliumus and prednisone. Leflunomide 
was held and should not be restarted as this medication is no 
longer needed. 

CHRONIC ISSUES were managed without any acute interventions, 
other home medications were continued as noted in premedication 
list. 

This patient was prescribed, or continued on, an opioid pain 
medication at the time of discharge (please see the attached 
medication list for details). As part of our safe opioid 
prescribing process, all patients are provided with an opioid 
risks and treatment resource education sheet and encouraged to 
discuss this therapy with their outpatient providers to 
determine if opioid pain medication is still indicated.

EXAMINATION:  RENAL TRANSPLANT U.S. LEFT

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with hx ESRD ___ diabetic nephropathy s/p failed
LRRT in ___ and active DDRT in ___ with progressive kidney failue ___ HTN.//
assess transplanted kidney

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale as well as color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images
of the renal transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Renal Doppler from ___

FINDINGS: 

The left transplant renal morphology is normal.  Specifically, the cortex is
of normal thickness.  There is mild increase in the echogenicity of the
transplant Kidney.  There is no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is
normal.  There is no hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.77 in the mid and
lower pole to 0.95 in the upper pole, previously ranging between 0.72 and
0.81.  The intrarenal artery in the upper pole shows markedly diminished
diastolic flow with elevated resistive index reaching 0.95.  There is a known
arteriovenous fistula at the inferior pole of the transplant Kidney.

The main renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke
and continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity of 65 cm
per second.  Vascularity is symmetric throughout the transplant. The
transplant renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

IMPRESSION:


1. There is no hydronephrosis within the transplant kidney in the left lower
quadrant.
2. Mildly elevated resistive index within the superior pole intrarenal
arteries of the transplant kidney with normal resistive indices within the mid
and inferior pole renal vessels.  Close attention on follow-up.
3. Known arteriovenous fistula at the inferior pole of the transplant kidney
is unchanged.
